summary: Carded from Fabio's report: a chat attachment handed to the in-app agent is a 512-wide thumbnail rendition, not the gallery card's real media file. Root cause proven by a byte-identical sha256 match against the card's .thumb.webp.

todo -> doing. Root cause proven by a byte-identical sha256 match: the staged attachment IS the card's .thumb.webp. The in-app card drag carries the thumbnail's bytes in dataTransfer.files, and MpiAgentChat's drop read only that, ignoring the application/mpi-media payload that names the real file. Ownership declared in files.json.

Shipped and validating. MpiAgentChat's drop now reads application/mpi-media before dataTransfer.files and attaches the card's real file; the decision is cardAttachmentSource() in js/utils/mediaActions.js. 4/4 new tests green and proven RED on the pre-fix handler; npm test 1752 tests 0 fail; lint clean; the transport run for real in Chromium attaches 768x1024 / 1549178 bytes where the bug staged 512x682. One check left and it is a human one: Chromium's synthesis of dataTransfer.files from a dragged is the mechanism itself and Playwright cannot reproduce it, so Fabio reloads the running app, drags a card onto the chat and checks the file size in %APPDATA%/Cubric Studio/agent/attachments/.

doing -> done. Fabio confirmed it in his running app: the staged attachment is att_974df319.png, PNG 768x1024, 1.47 MB - the card's own file, where the bug staged a 512x682 WebP. That was the one check no harness here could make, because Chromium's synthesis of dataTransfer.files from a dragged IS the mechanism. Shipped in 712c3ff2, on origin/master; no run fired on that sha (a peer pushed it with their own commit) but its direct descendant ed9d4a51 carries the code unchanged and concluded success. Left behind, uncarded: a VIDEO card dropped on the chat still attaches its poster frame.
